comparison: Perfect alignment on methods claims (C96-C111). Both accept the methodological descriptions as adequate. Peer reviewer initially requested improved figure descriptions, which were addressed in revision and then accepted.

Strong agreement on neuronal imaging quality (C39-C41, C54, C83). OpenEval notes clear visualization but suggests quantitative resolution measurements would strengthen claims. Peer reviewer accepts high-quality imaging of dense brain tissue without requesting additional quantification.

Both accept cost-effectiveness context (C58-C61). OpenEval notes cost claims are somewhat subjective and lack specific citations. Peer reviewer explicitly affirms the cost-effectiveness motivation as valid, stating RIM-Deep enables 'cost-effective imaging' as alternative to 'expensive new equipment.'

Agreement on large-scale imaging capability (C42-C44, C84). OpenEval supports claims but suggests quantitative metrics for positioning and alignment would strengthen them. Peer reviewer accepts the large-sample imaging capability after revisions addressed previous concerns.

Both support stroke model application (C47-C50, C55). OpenEval notes 'significantly reduced vessel density' claim lacks quantitative analysis or statistical testing, making it qualitative. Peer reviewer accepts high-quality images from all samples including stroke model without requesting statistical analysis.

Agreement on depth extension claims (C32-C34, C52). OpenEval supports the 2mm to 5mm improvement but notes lack of statistical analysis details (no p-values for 'no significant difference' claim). Peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges '2-fold increase' as 'significant enhancement' without requesting additional statistics.

Both affirm overall significance of RIM-Deep (C56, C62, C80, C82). OpenEval supports versatility and contribution claims based on multi-platform demonstrations. Peer reviewer confirms the technique is 'useful' with 'potential to significantly enhance imaging quality' on 'low budget' for 'wide range of researchers.'

Agreement on technical limitations (C71-C74). OpenEval accepts these as honest assessment of current limitations with awareness of emerging solutions. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts by not challenging these stated limitations in final acceptance.

Both support RIM-Deep system design (C23-C27, C89-C95). OpenEval finds design principles clearly articulated and visually documented. Peer reviewer affirms development and utility, stating RIM-Deep 'has the potential to significantly enhance imaging quality' and technical design is accepted without critique.

Agreement on future directions and acknowledged limitations (C77-C79, C81, C66-C70). OpenEval accepts these as reasonable suggestions with appropriate citations. Peer reviewer's acceptance indicates these acknowledged limitations are reasonable and don't undermine core contributions.

Both support cross-platform and multi-method validation (C35-C38, C53, C56, C104-C105). OpenEval notes consistency across methods and platforms strengthens findings. Peer reviewer confirms authors 'tested their method on different microscopic setups' and provided 'detailed comparison' across 3 clearing methods, addressing initial weaknesses.

Agreement on RIM-Deep design and rationale (C23-C31 vs C23-C27, C89-C95). OpenEval supports design principles with visual documentation. Peer reviewer accepts the system development, confirming it 'describes a useful technique' with accepted technical components.

Both accept background on existing approaches and limitations (C13-C22 overlap with broader C1-C22, C51, C87-C88). OpenEval finds well-cited background establishing technology gap. Peer reviewer accepts problem statement about imaging depth limitations without challenge.

Agreement on optical principles background (C5-C12 within broader C1-C22, C87-C88). OpenEval accepts well-established optical principles with appropriate citations. Peer reviewer accepts contextual claims about optical aberrations and imaging depth limitations.

Both accept tissue clearing background (C1-C4 within C1-C22, C87-C88). OpenEval notes these are established facts with appropriate citations representing accepted knowledge. Peer reviewer does not challenge this background material.

Divergence on wide-field microscopy application (C63-C66 vs C64-C65, C85). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature without experimental validation. Peer reviewer accepts broader applicability claims after authors tested on different microscopic setups, though wide-field specifically may not have been demonstrated.

Partial agreement on summary capabilities (C82-C86 vs C62, C80, C82). OpenEval supports demonstrated capabilities (C82-C84) but rates overall as UNCERTAIN due to speculative claims about two-photon and wide-field extensions (C85-C86). Peer reviewer focuses on affirmed significance without addressing speculative extensions.

Divergence on future applicability (C85 in both). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting two-photon and wide-field extensions are proposed but not demonstrated. Peer reviewer accepts compatibility claims after multi-setup testing, though specific modalities may differ.

Agreement on scope limitations (C67-C71 overlap at C71). OpenEval accepts honest acknowledgment of limitations including limited scope to neural tissues. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts by not challenging stated limitations.

Agreement on abstract-level problem statement (C87-C89 vs C87-C88 in broader context). OpenEval supports accurate description of limitations and development goal. Peer reviewer accepts problem statement about imaging depth limitations due to optical aberrations.
